description: The constant baseline ignores the input features. It returns the training set's class proportions for classification or its mean target value for regression, showing what can be predicted without using the measurements.

CatBoost builds an ensemble of decision trees through gradient boosting, adding trees that improve the current predictions. It supports numerical and categorical features for classification and regression.
LightGBM is a gradient boosting method that builds decision trees using binned feature values. It grows each tree by splitting the leaf with the largest reduction in the training objective.

KNN predicts from the training examples closest to a new sample in feature space. The benchmark uses equally weighted neighbors, taking their class votes for classification or averaging their target values for regression.

Logistic regression learns a weighted combination of the input features and turns it into class probabilities. For continuous targets, this entry uses ridge regression, a linear model with a penalty that keeps its coefficients from becoming too large.

Random Forest grows decision trees on bootstrap samples of the training data, considering a random subset of features at each split. It averages their class probabilities for classification or their numerical predictions for regression.

XGBoost combines decision trees through gradient boosting, adding trees to improve the ensemble's predictions. Its training objective includes penalties on tree complexity, alongside the loss for classification or regression.

Extra Trees averages the predictions of many decision trees. Each tree considers randomly chosen features and split thresholds, adding more randomness than a conventional random forest when learning a classification or regression task.

This multilayer perceptron uses AutoGluon's PyTorch implementation for tabular classification and regression. It passes the input features through fully connected hidden layers with nonlinear activations to learn the prediction function.

RealMLP is a multilayer perceptron trained on each dataset for classification or regression. It combines numerical preprocessing with a carefully chosen network and training setup, using defaults selected across a broad collection of tabular tasks.

TabM, by Yandex Research, trains a group of multilayer perceptrons together for tabular classification or regression, with most of their weights shared. Each input produces several predictions that are combined, giving the model an ensemble structure without storing and training a full set of separate networks.

_doc: Advisory post-cap features x train-row observations from the 2026-08 full-grid run. None are enforced: every legacy OOM/model-limit cell is retried under the new memory handling, and only a newly observed OOM triggers sample fallback. MITRA's fixed 8k allocation and TabPFN-Wide's inference batching have changed; TabFM's observed fit boundary is not treated as certain either.
description: MITRA is a pretrained model for tabular classification and regression that learns from a mixture of synthetic datasets generated by different rules. It uses labelled examples as context for new predictions, and AutoGluon's implementation also adapts its pretrained weights to the target dataset through fine-tuning.

TabPFN v2, by Prior Labs, is a pretrained transformer for classification and regression on tables. It takes labelled training rows as context and predicts new rows without training a separate neural network from scratch for each dataset.

TabPFN 2.5, by Prior Labs, uses a pretrained transformer to make predictions from labelled examples, extending the v2 family to wider tables. Its default classifier includes pretraining on real datasets, while its default regressor is pretrained on synthetic data only.

TabPFN 3, by Prior Labs, is a transformer pretrained on synthetic prediction tasks. For classification or regression on a new table, it uses the labelled training rows as examples to guide its predictions rather than learning the task from scratch.

TabPFN 3.5, the latest version by Prior Labs, is pretrained on synthetic tables and uses labelled examples as context for new predictions. A single shared checkpoint handles both classification and regression, rather than using separate pretrained models for the two tasks.

TabPFN-Wide continues pre-training TabPFN 2 on synthetic tables with many features and few samples, a setting common in omics. This classification model uses the wide-v2-8k checkpoint to work with wider inputs than the original model.

_doc: Regular wide-v2-5k checkpoint with a three-member inference ensemble and the checkpoint-native one-feature grouping.
description: TabPFN-Wide continues pre-training TabPFN 2 on synthetic tables with many features and few samples, a setting common in omics. This TabPFN-Wide configuration uses the wide-v2-5k checkpoint, pretrained for classification with many features and few samples. It averages three inference variants while keeping the checkpoint's original feature grouping.

TabFM is Google's pretrained model for classification and regression on tables containing numerical and categorical columns. It predicts from labelled training rows supplied as context, using sampled groups of rows and features when needed, rather than updating its model weights for each new dataset.

TabDPT is a tabular foundation model by Layer6 AI pretrained on real datasets using self-supervised prediction tasks. For a new classification or regression problem, it retrieves relevant labelled rows and uses them as context to predict new rows without updating its weights on that dataset.

TabICL v2 is a transformer pretrained on varied synthetic tables for classification and regression. It uses labelled training rows as context when predicting new rows, with attention designed to handle larger tables without requiring equally long tables throughout pretraining.

GeneICL is built for prediction from bulk gene expression profiles. It compresses the gene measurements with principal component analysis, then uses a pretrained recurrent network to learn from labelled examples without updating its weights for each new task.

FTFM-1 builds cell representations from factorized row and column representations, then predicts classes from labelled training rows supplied as context. This benchmark uses its released eight-member ensemble with sequential views. Its pretraining configuration includes real and synthetic data, so results are flagged for possible training-data overlap.

Causilo, by Nums AI, is pretrained on synthetic tables and uses labelled examples as context for classification or regression. It processes relationships across rows and columns, combining information about individual features with patterns shared by samples.

Kumo Tabular, by NVIDIA, learns from synthetic tables before it is applied to a new dataset. It builds representations of columns and rows, then uses labelled examples as context for classification or regression; this benchmark uses the medium-sized model. The released default recipe selects at most 500 features; this benchmark removes that selection step and evaluates the full feature budget.

Kumo Tabular Large is the released large tabular foundation model from NVIDIA for classification and regression. It uses labelled training rows as context without updating its weights. This benchmark uses its eight-member ensemble, processes members sequentially, and lets the benchmark control feature and sample budgets. The released default recipe selects at most 500 features; this benchmark removes that selection step and evaluates the full feature budget.

Seldon, by Neuralk-AI, is a 213.5-million-parameter transformer pretrained only on synthetic tables. It compresses cells into row representations and uses labelled training rows as context for classification without updating its weights. This benchmark keeps its released eight-member inference ensemble and lets the benchmark control feature and sample budgets. The released recipe normally selects at most 500 features; this benchmark removes that selection step and evaluates the full feature budget.

Seldon-Mini is Neuralk-AI's 27.4-million-parameter classification model, pretrained only on synthetic tables. It uses labelled examples as context without updating its weights. This benchmark keeps its released four-member inference ensemble and lets the benchmark control feature and sample budgets. The released recipe normally selects at most 500 features; this benchmark removes that selection step and evaluates the full feature budget.

LimiX-2 is pretrained on synthetic tables generated from causal models. It learns relationships between features and targets through masked prediction, then uses labelled rows as context to predict classes or numerical values in a new table.

_doc: AutoML reference, not a ranked peer: runs AutoGluon's native extreme preset without overriding its portfolio, under the benchmark's one-hour per-unit time limit.
description: AutoGluon automates tabular learning by training multiple models and combining their predictions in ensembles. Here it runs its native extreme preset within a one-hour budget as a separate AutoML reference.
